images.scene: Setting: a small family-owned neighborhood shop on a street corner in Brazil in the late 1970s, corrugated steel roll-up shutter door, tiled sidewalk, worn wooden counter, shelves of goods, a steel thermos of coffee, the shopkeeper in a plain work apron. Pre-dawn, the street dark and empty. TWO shopfronts side by side on the same plaster wall, seen straight on from across the narrow street, filling the frame from the left edge to the right edge. The LEFT shop is OPEN: shutter raised, warm light glowing from inside over the counter, the thermos on the counter. The RIGHT shop is CLOSED: its corrugated steel shutter pulled all the way down, dark, padlocked. Above the open shop hangs an old weathered hand-painted wooden shop sign board with faded illegible lettering (just worn smudged shapes, no readable words), and above the closed shop a torn old poster; the same old plaster wall continues ABOVE both shops with cracks and stains, so the building clearly goes on upward, and only at the very top of the frame the wall is evenly lit and pale. The sidewalk and street in front are completely EMPTY. Camera close, the two shopfronts large in the lower three quarters. NO fog, NO mist, NO haze and NO smoke anywhere inside the scene: the scene itself is crisp and clean with normal contrast; only the narrow band at the very top of the frame is a pale, evenly lit, continuous surface (plaster wall or overcast sky) with nothing crossing it. THE TOP BAND IS A HARD REQUIREMENT: that top fifth must be ONE single continuous evenly-lit pale surface spanning the FULL width, with NOTHING crossing it at all: no roofline, no beam, no ceiling, no shelf, no sign, no branch, no head, no edge of any object.
